risks.proof: A clear photo of the TV’s back cover/inside power supply board showing the blown component, plus a short video of the TV attempting to power on (standby light, any backlight flash).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / worst-case power failure (not just transformer).

risks.risk: Screen/panel may be damaged even if power supply is the issue (common with impact or failed backlight).
risks.proof: Video showing the TV powered on with a flashlight test (shine torch at the screen to check for faint image) and/or a clear power-on display.

risks.risk: Brand/model and exact size may be different from the seller’s claim, affecting parts availability and value.
risks.proof: Photo of the label/sticker on the back showing brand, model number, and screen size.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the lowest end for an unknown/possibly non-working small TV.

risks.risk: Possible scam/low-quality listing: photos may not match the claimed unit or condition.
risks.proof: Photo of the TV with a visible handwritten note (your name + today’s date) and a close-up of the model label.
risks.if_unproven: Priced conservatively as a risky non-working item.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the TV back label/sticker (brand + exact model number + size).
Photo(s) of the inside power supply/transformer area showing the blown part (or burn mark) and the board.
Short video of the TV powering on (standby light behavior, any backlight flash).
Flashlight test video (torch at an angle to the screen) to confirm whether there’s any image.
response.reason: From photo 0, the TV’s brand/model and the claimed transformer damage are not verifiable, and the screen/power status is unclear. Without proof, the item must be treated as worst-case non-working, so a reliable price can’t be set yet.
